evidence: Identifies both redelivery and concurrency schedules: after the update commits, `Publish`/`Record` failure leaves no inbox row, and concurrent deliveries can both see false; requires the unique message claim and aggregate transition to commit in one transaction.

Shows commit-before-publish loss via a crash after `UpdateAggregate` commits and before `Publish`, and publish-before-inbox exposure via `Record` failure after publication; requires aggregate update, inbox completion, and outbox record to commit atomically with relay publication later.
Requires “an event identity stable for the input message” in the atomic outbox and downstream deduplication of that stable identity, explicitly rejecting new IDs on ambiguous outcomes.
States acknowledgment is safe only after the durable transaction commits and that failed or unknown `Ack` redelivery must become a durable no-op; it does not claim end-to-end exactly-once delivery.
Explicitly quantifies “15 `Apply` executions and 45 publish attempts” and requires one retry owner, an end-to-end deadline, transient-only retries, and reconciliation of ambiguous outcomes.
Does not claim exactly-once processing; instead it requires replay to be a durable no-op and repeated outbox publication to be deduplicated.
Does not recommend early acknowledgment; it explicitly says acknowledgment is safe only after the transaction commits.
Does not recommend merely adding retries/backoff; it requires one bounded retry owner and removes retry amplification through atomic inbox/outbox state and stable identity.
verdict.summary: The candidate satisfies all five required distributed-correctness findings and does not exhibit any forbidden outcome.
